:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.5.13`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noXorAsExponentiation`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**warning**](/reference/diagnostics#warning).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`unicorn/no-xor-as-exponentiation`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/main/docs/rules/no-xor-as-exponentiation.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noXorAsExponentiation": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow the bitwise XOR operator where exponentiation was likely intended.

In JavaScript, `^` is the bitwise XOR operator, not exponentiation.
Developers coming from languages like Lua, Julia, R, or MATLAB, or from
math notation, often expect `^` to mean "to the power of", so `2 ^ 32`
silently evaluates to `34` instead of `4294967296`. The actual
exponentiation operator is `**`.

This rule flags `^` between two decimal integer literals, which is
almost always this mistake. Hexadecimal, octal, and binary literals
(such as `0xFF ^ 8`) and any non-literal operands (such as
`flags ^ MASK`) are ignored, since those are far more likely to be
intentional bitwise XOR.

## Examples

### Invalid

```js
const kibibyte = 2 ^ 10; // 8, not 1024
```

### Valid

```js
const kibibyte = 2 ** 10;
const cube = 3 ** 3;
const masked = flags ^ MASK;
const bits = 0xFF ^ 8;
```
